newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger to seek an end to Giddings defense.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger to seek an end to Giddings defense.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Monday it will seek a special meeting of Giddings & Lewis Inc shareholders, where it will ask the them to remove Giddings & Lewis' current board of directors.

Harnischfeger said that, if successful, it would then seek to have Giddings' "poison pill" takeover defense dismantled, so shareholders could accept Harnischfeger's $19 a share tender offer for the Fond du Lac, Wisconsin-based machine tool and industrial automation products manufacturer.
Milwaukee-based Harnischfeger on Monday officially commenced the tender offer, which it values at $747 million, including assumption of Giddings' debt.
Harnischfeger officials also told reporters they had expected the company's stock to fall Monday, as it has.

"The stock was off before we even had a chance to talk to people (about the offer), so it's obviously a knee-jerk reaction," Harnischfeger chief executive officer Jeffery Grade said in a conference call with reporters.
"Over time ... we expect that market to come back, if not become appreciative," after Harnischfeger talks more with its shareholders and analysts, Grade said.
Harnischfeger shares were down 3-5/8 at 41-3/4 Monday, while Giddings shares were up 6-5/8 at 20-1/4.
Grade said he thought Giddings shares were up above the $19 tender offer because of speculation that a bidder will emerge with a higher offer.
"We haven't seen a large line develop out there, but it could happen and I'm sure somebody is guessing that's what's going to happen and they may be terribly disappointed. I don't know," Grade said.
